name: mirin
issue: Most supermarket mirin (aji-mirin) is sweetened with corn syrup and may contain sulphites; key 'mirin' only tags alcohol
suggest: alcohol, corn (add note: check label for corn syrup)

name: panza de cerdo
issue: Pork with empty key; pork filter will not catch it
suggest: pork (needs a pork meat key, e.g. 'pork')

name: cerdo picado
issue: Ground pork with empty key; pork filter will not catch it

name: zanahoria y colinabo
issue: Store-bought pickles; brine vinegar may contain sulphites

name: salsa de caramelo
issue: Bottled Vietnamese caramel sauce (nuoc mau) sometimes contains added sulphites/colourings; key is sugar only
suggest: sugar; add note 'check label' or keep as homemade

name: salsa de pescado
issue: Some fish sauce brands contain wheat/hydrolysed protein; key tags fish only
suggest: fish (+ note: some brands contain wheat)

name: mantequilla
issue: Steps 3-4 depend on browning milk solids; a dairy-free swap (olive oil / refined coconut oil) cannot brown, and 'cook until it smells nutty' will just overheat the oil. Misleading for milk-free users
suggest: add substitution note: with oil, fry sage only and skip browning step

name: pasta rellena
issue: Step 6 tosses stuffed pasta that is not in the ingredient list; filled pasta almost always contains wheat, egg and milk (often also nuts/meat) and is invisible to the filter
suggest: add ingredient 'pasta rellena' with k=pasta (+egg, milk tags) or a warning note

name: ajo confitado
issue: Garlic confit is garlic in oil; homemade stored at room temp is a botulism risk; store-bought may contain sulphites/citric acid
suggest: allium; add safety note: keep refrigerated, use within a few days

name: aceitunas negras
issue: Jarred/canned black olives frequently contain sulphites/ferrous gluconate; empty key

name: alcaparras
issue: Capers in vinegar brine (often wine vinegar) may contain sulphites; empty key

name: caldo (tip 3)
issue: Tip suggests Tuscan version with 'caldo' (stock); store-bought stock often contains celery, wheat, soy, milk; not in ingredient list
suggest: note in tip or add stock ingredient with celery tag

name: pulpo
issue: Octopus keyed as 'squid'; allergen (mollusc) correct but substitutions offered for squid may not fit

name: pescado de roca
issue: Step 1 makes broth with prawn heads and shells; someone who swaps out prawns for shellfish allergy must also leave shells out of the broth, and rockfish broth mixes can include crustaceans from fishmongers
suggest: add note: shellfish-free version must omit shells from broth

name: pecorino romano
issue: Whole method (cheese paste emulsified off heat) depends on real pecorino; the milk-free swap (nutritional yeast + salt at 0.45x) will not emulsify or form a sauce, so steps 3 and 5 are misleading for a dairy-free cook
suggest: milk (keyed ok); add note to substitution that the sauce will be a starchy coating, not an emulsion

name: tonnarelli o espagueti
issue: Steps rely on starchy pasta water to emulsify; gluten-free/corn pasta releases less starch and overcooks fast, so 'drain 2 minutes early' can leave it mushy
suggest: wheat (keyed ok); add GF note: drain 1 min early per pasta substitute rule

name: salsa Worcestershire
issue: Keyed as anchovy (fish only); UK-recipe Worcestershire uses malt vinegar (barley/gluten) and some brands contain soy; may contain sulphites
suggest: fish, wheat (malt vinegar), soy? , sulphite; needs its own 'worcestershire' key

name: mostaza de Dijon
issue: Dijon is made with white wine/verjuice; commonly contains sulphites. Key mustard tags only mustard

name: yemas de huevo
issue: Raw yolks; tip covers pasteurized yolks. With an egg swap (aquafaba) the emulsion is weaker; fine. Raw-egg note should also mention pregnancy/immunocompromised

name: ron oscuro
issue: Rum with empty key; alcohol filter will not catch it (and some dark rums contain added caramel colour/sulphites)

name: cera de abeja
issue: Mold coating is beeswax PLUS an equal weight of butter (in the note), but the row has no key; a milk-free cook who swaps ing 1 still uses butter on the molds
suggest: milk (or split butter for molds into its own row with k=butter)

name: vino marsala
issue: Fortified wine with empty key; not caught by alcohol or sulphite filters

name: manteca o mantequilla
issue: Keyed lard (pork) only, but the name offers butter as an alternative (milk); a milk-allergic user choosing butter is not warned
suggest: pork, milk (or split into lard and butter rows)

name: fruta confitada
issue: Candied fruit keyed as sugar only; commercial candied peel/fruit usually contains sulphites and glucose/corn syrup, often colourings

name: chocolate negro
issue: Keyed darkchocolate (soy only); many dark chocolates contain milk fat or are made on shared lines with milk/nuts

name: aceite (para freír)
issue: Unspecified frying oil with empty key; could be peanut oil. Name a neutral non-allergen oil
suggest: specify 'aceite neutro (girasol/canola)'; or peanut if peanut oil is used

name: huevo
issue: Egg is used only as glue for sealing the shells (step 4), role 'binder'. Egg-free cooks can seal with water or flax gel; binder substitutes list works but note should say 'for sealing'

name: vinagre de vino tinto
issue: Wine vinegar with empty key; contains sulphites (and traces of alcohol)

name: pasas
issue: Raisins with empty key; dried fruit (especially golden raisins) is commonly treated with sulphites

name: aceitunas verdes
issue: Jarred olives may contain sulphites/preservatives; empty key

name: alcaparras
issue: Capers in vinegar brine may contain sulphites; empty key

name: yemas de huevo
issue: Dish is an egg emulsion made off the heat; the egg 'set' substitute (silken tofu + cornstarch) needs heat to thicken, so steps 4-6 ('off the heat', 'you'll get scrambled eggs') are misleading for an egg-free cook
suggest: egg (keyed ok); add substitute note: with tofu/cornstarch, return pan to low heat until it thickens

name: guanciale
issue: Tip 3 recommends guanciale over 'tocino' (bacon), both pork; no issue for keys, but cured guanciale/pancetta may contain sulphites/nitrites and sometimes dextrose/lactose in commercial cures

name: salchicha de Toulouse
issue: Keyed as 'chorizo' (pork, nightshade). Toulouse sausage has no paprika, so nightshade is a false positive; commercial sausages often contain sulphites (UK) and sometimes rusk/wheat or milk powder
suggest: pork (+ sulphite, wheat if commercial); needs a plain 'sausage' key

name: corteza de cerdo
issue: Pork rind with empty key; pork filter will not catch it

name: huevos

name: huevos
